evidence.claim: Hot signers can pass arbitrary values for function parameters that have no calldata-check coverage, because checkCalldata only validates the index ranges that were explicitly whitelisted.
evidence.support_reason: checkCalldata (475-504) only iterates the stored Index ranges for (target, selector) and requires each stored slice hash to match; any calldata bytes outside those ranges are never inspected. executeWhitelisted (715-726) and executeWhitelistedBatch (733-755) call checkCalldata then _execute, so a hot signer can supply arbitrary values in uncovered parameter slots. _addCalldataCheck (1034-1155) permits adding a single narrow range (e.g. startIndex 4, endIndex 36) without requiring full coverage, and _removeCalldataCheck (1193-1243) can drop a range, leaving the parameter unconstrained.
preconditions: hot signer holds HOT_SIGNER_ROLE (trusted role per README)
safe owners whitelisted a function with only partial parameter coverage (or removed a range)
target contract's uncovered parameter is security-relevant (e.g. recipient, amount, spender)
evidence.known_issue_match: If the hot signers are malicious or compromised, they can execute transactions to compromise the system if neither recovery spells or the guardian are used; also Timelock.sol:36-39 'incorrectly formed whitelisted calldata can allow safe owners the ability to steal funds'
